speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Heading: on contragredient Lie algebras
summary: Only a dated heading and the title \ru{О контраградиентных алгебрах Ли} survive before the next dated heading, 21 September, on P000981. The catalog range extends into P000982, but those mathematical notes belong to the following meeting. No mathematical claim is assigned to this heading-only record.

speaker: S. I. Gelfand
title: Reading list and finite-dimensional Lie theory
summary: The meeting begins with a reading list on highest-weight modules and Kac--Moody algebras. Macdonald's June 1981 Bourbaki lecture can be identified exactly as expos\'e 577, \emph{Affine Lie algebras and modular forms}; Humphreys' contribution is the 1980 LNM 831 chapter, pp.~72--103 \citep{macdonald1981affine,humphreys1980highest}. The intervening exposition, explicitly marked I.~M.~G., reviews roots, the Weyl group, Chevalley--Serre relations, highest weights and characters. A speculative Lorentz/neutrino aside has insufficient mathematical specification. The content ends at Rudakov's heading on P000984, not at the catalog endpoint. Several mistakes are in the notebook itself: the order of the symmetric group, the root/weight lattice distinction and omitted off-diagonal restrictions.

speaker: A. N. Rudakov
title: Contragredient Lie algebras and Cartan-matrix types
summary: Rudakov starts on P000984 with generators, relations, an enlarged Cartan space and a maximal ideal avoiding that space. He then removes redundant central directions and states the finite/affine/indefinite trichotomy for indecomposable generalized Cartan matrices. The literal affine alternative is internally contradictory. At the top of P000986 Gelfand adds the two Rogers--Ramanujan identities. The arrow returning to S.~I.~Gelfand on that page marks the next record. The historical construction should be compared with \citet[Chapter II]{kac1968graded} and \citet[\S2]{macdonald1981affine}; the latter's Serre-presentation convention must not silently replace the maximal-ideal definition for nonsymmetrizable matrices.

speaker: S. I. Gelfand
title: Verma embeddings and a root-multiplicity question
summary: The return arrow on P000986 begins a review of Verma modules and the Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand criterion for embeddings. The formulas mix the notebook's unshifted highest weight with a negative rho shift and do not delimit the finite-dimensional semisimple scope of the quoted theorem. At the top of P000987, Gelfand asks for root-space dimensions and independent words for general Cartan matrices. The next dated heading starts Seifert's talk. The multiplicity question is indexed, but neither efficiency nor a uniform positive combinatorial formula is demanded in the surviving wording; no artificial open conjecture is extracted.

speaker: Benedict Seifert
title: Transformation-group geometry and a Bruhat-type decomposition
summary: The actual heading is on P000987 and includes a question mark after the Russian surname and the affiliation Paris. Fixed sets of pointwise stabilizers define a closure geometry; the speaker builds flags, proposes four axioms and asserts a double-coset decomposition. The closest publication is Seifert's \emph{Transitivity Properties, Bruhat Decomposition and Tits Systems for Transformation Groups}, received 5 March 1983, published June 1984. Its exact axiom list could not be read in this run, so the identification is partial. Seifert's later paper explicitly distinguishes its new tree transitivity and proof from the earlier work \citep[Introduction and reference S.1]{seifert1986highly}. Gelfand's three concrete double-coset exercises occur on P000989 before the Zelevinsky heading.

speaker: A. V. Zelevinsky
title: Equioriented type-A quiver orbits and their geometry
summary: The actual exposition begins in the lower part of P000989 and explicitly reports \citet{abeasisdelfrakraft1981geometry}, whose September 1981 issue and receipt date of 1 April 1981 precede the meeting. It explains the finite orbit classification, rank invariants, good singularities of orbit closures and the determinantal special case. The closing analogy with Schubert geometry has a precise later realization in Zelevinsky's 1985 paper; the accompanying p-adic multiplicity connection must be distinguished from that purely geometric identification. The next dated heading on P000990 begins Kirillov's talk.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Rank-two Serre presentations, free Lie dimensions and interlacing arrays
summary: Kirillov asks about the two-generator Lie algebra with two Serre relations, gives the multigraded Witt formula before relations, identifies a Catalan specialization, and passes to the enveloping algebra and a Hilbert-series logarithm. A bare lexicographic word list does not specify a reduction algorithm. Gelfand then asks for the number of integer interlacing arrays with four fixed top entries. The latter counts a basis of one irreducible representation, not distinct representations of that highest weight. The record ends on P000991; the next meeting starts on P000992.

speaker: A. S. Schwarz
title: Supergravity as the geometry of a real supersurface
summary: Schwarz treats real \((4|4)\)-dimensional supersurfaces in \(\mathbb C^{4|2}\), a holomorphic volume-preserving pseudogroup, the odd complex tangent distribution and its Levi form. The action is written as a delta-function surface integral; a preliminary exponent on P000993 is explicitly replaced by the Jacobian-corrected expression on P000994. An SCR structure retains a determinant normalization absent from ordinary CR data. The October 1981 announcement is identified bibliographically, and the detailed formulas are verified in \citet[\S3, pp.~44--48]{schwarz1982supergravity}, received 15 February 1982. The broader field-space-democracy work is not confused with this exact Levi determinant formula. The record ends before the 23 November heading on P000995.

speaker: A. V. Zelevinsky
title: Verma-module multiplicities and Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials
summary: The actual section begins on P000995 and continues onto P000996, before Beilinson speaks. It recalls highest-weight modules and finite-length Verma modules, reduces composition multiplicities to a regular integral Weyl orbit, and reports the proved Kazhdan--Lusztig multiplicity conjecture. A subsequent coefficient interpretation anticipates the separate Jantzen-filtration discussion. The catalog page span includes earlier Schwarz material; it is not a mathematical boundary.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Category O and restricted contragredient duality
summary: The named intervention occupies P000996, between the coefficient question and S. Gelfand. It introduces category \(\mathcal O\), restricted duality, and the dual Verma module as preparation for the Jantzen filtration. The notebook confuses the sign of the locally nilpotent nilradical and does not spell out the anti-involution required for a duality preserving highest-weight category \(\mathcal O\).

speaker: S. I. Gelfand
title: Contravariant forms, Jantzen layers and deformation directions
summary: The named section starts at the foot of P000996 and ends above the new Zelevinsky heading on P000997. It describes the contravariant form, identifies Verma modules through PBW vectors, deforms the weight by \(t\rho\), and introduces the order-of-vanishing filtration. It asks whether changing \(\rho\) preserves layer multiplicities and links coefficients to Schubert geometry. Moving lifts, normalization of polynomial degrees, and the distinction between ordinary and intersection cohomology require explicit repair.

speaker: A. V. Zelevinsky
title: Finite-dimensional weight multiplicities and affine Weyl polynomials
summary: The section begins near the foot of P000997. Gelfand inserts the type-A alternant character formula and a Cauchy-determinant exercise. Zelevinsky then identifies weight multiplicities with values of affine Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials, followed by an incompletely specified extension to all Kac--Moody algebras. The latter is kept apart from the finite-dimensional Verma-module multiplicity theorem.

speaker: A. G. Elashvili
title: Primitive enveloping algebras and Frobenius semidirect products
summary: The actual intervention occupies the lower part of P000998. It asks Jacobson\textquotesingle s primitivity question, excludes nonzero semisimple and nilpotent examples, gives affine and binary-cubic semidirect products, and asserts a restricted classification with a further construction method. The exact 1982 announcement identifies the older Ooms criterion and supplies the missing reductive hypotheses; its full classification is broader than the notebook\textquotesingle s two examples.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Nonstandard analysis, relaxation oscillations and surreal sign sequences
summary: The section begins on P000999 and continues to the Krichever heading on P001000. It reports Cartier\textquotesingle s November 1981 Bourbaki exposition of Reeb\textquotesingle s methods, gives the van der Pol singular limit and its Rayleigh form, and sketches Cartier\textquotesingle s random-element quotient using a zero-one finitely additive measure. It then introduces surreal numbers through arrow sequences. The ultrapower and surreal field are distinct constructions; the open-interval probability codomain and finite-arrow halving rule require mathematical emendation.

speaker: I. M. Krichever
title: An elliptic matrix-function fragment
summary: Only the bottom of P001000 is headed Krichever. It names joint work with Brazovskii and Dzyaloshinskii, writes an unspecified ascending union, and displays a sigma-product matrix function on an elliptic curve with a divisor-sum condition. Krichever\textquotesingle s 1983 survey, \S1.3, identifies a closely matching algebra of matrix Baker--Akhiezer functions; the filtration remains a reconstruction. The 1982 joint Peierls paper confirms the collaboration, but supplies only thematic context for the surviving fragment.

title: Year 1982
summary: The catalog's undated year heading marks the transition to calendar year 1982 within the academic year 1981--82. It supplies no independent mathematical assertion. Its catalog page range overlaps Müller's dated lecture and must not create a duplicate talk or duplicate occurrence.

speaker: Werner Müller
title: Lattice gravity and curvature of piecewise flat spaces
summary: Müller reports joint work with Jeff Cheeger and Robert Schrader. A formal path-integral motivation leads to Regge's hinge curvature, nondegenerate smooth triangulations, convergence of curvature measures, higher Lipschitz--Killing curvatures, finite-dimensional metric spaces of simplices, and an integral-geometric proof idea. Gelfand asks which curvature actions have lower-order field equations. The source explicitly separates curvature convergence from the still unclear convergence of the equations. The catalog range extends through P001007; the next dated heading actually starts at P001006. Several faithful mathematical errors require emendation, especially the heat sign, the Euler-form trace, and the edge-length Jacobian.

speaker: V. L. Ginzburg [catalog attribution]
title: Hamiltonian actions and the moment map
summary: A short announcement records the definition of a Hamiltonian Lie-group action and its moment map, including infinitesimal equivariance and Poisson compatibility. The manuscript heading says only Ginzburg; the initials are those of the supplied catalog and are not independently established by the page. No additional theorem or unpublished program is recoverable. This content ends before the dated Arnold heading on P001007.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Integral geometry and lattice analogues
summary: Arnold compares the parallel-body polynomial, curvature integrals, projection averages, and Euler-characteristic Crofton formulas, then proposes their lattice analogues and refers to McMullen's Vancouver congress lecture. The lattice discussion states normalized-volume and quotient-lattice ideas, not a fully quantified discrete replacement for every continuous formula. This heading precedes Gelfand's Macdonald-book intervention on the physical page, although the catalog numbers put record 548 first.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: A partition complement identity and Guillemin's symplectic cones
summary: Gelfand gives a combinatorial exercise from Macdonald's book and its generating-function corollary, then introduces symplectic cones from work of Guillemin on Weyl asymptotics. The partition identity is identifiable exactly; its written corollary omits a conjugation and an inverse argument. The cone discussion introduces the subject resumed under Arnold's heading in record 550. The surviving notes state no final new spectral asymptotic theorem.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Contact cones, Weyl quantization and axiomatic operator algebras
summary: Arnold's intervention identifies the contact quotient of a symplectic cone. The ensuing exposition gives a Weyl kernel and axioms for complex-order operator classes: symbolic composition, asymptotic completeness, boundedness, compactness, trace-class thresholds, detection of principal symbols, splitting, and holomorphic order families. The connection with Guillemin's later axiomatic Weyl-algebra paper is identifiable, but the original 1985 article was not available in full during this audit. Local uniqueness, global quantization, and spectral conclusions must be kept separate.

speaker: Robert MacPherson
title: Proposed topics: perverse sheaves and bivariant theories
summary: The handwritten English explicitly introduces titles of a paper he would speak about. One diagram joins perverse sheaves, holonomic differential modules, and characteristic varieties; another proposes a theory attached to maps with homology and cohomology as its endpoints. These are substantive identifiable announcements, but the page does not document a completed lecture or proofs. The second topic matches the already published Fulton--MacPherson bivariant theory.

speaker: Dusa McDuff
title: Canonical classes of volume-preserving diffeomorphism groups
summary: McDuff constructs the homotopy fiber of the discrete-to-topological comparison, the universal transverse volume foliation, and its compactly supported cohomology classes. She records a torus test, the parity of the top class for spheres, and the opposite parity of a secondary class on Euclidean space. These claims match her 1983 paper, whose author bibliography reproduces its abstract; the full proofs were not obtained. Fuchs's interjection occurs inside this discussion and has its own catalog record.

speaker: D. B. Fuchs
title: A subgroup-fibration analogy during McDuff's talk
summary: Fuchs contributes the familiar subgroup fibration and a heuristic about a very dense subgroup having an infinitesimal fundamental domain. The homotopy fiber is the mathematically reliable object here; the naive quotient for the identity map from a group with discrete topology cannot serve as its replacement. This is an intervention, not a separate developed lecture. Its source position follows the beginning of McDuff's record 553.

speaker: John Milnor
title: Homology of Lie groups made discrete
summary: Milnor asks how the homology of a Lie group changes after forgetting its topology. The mod-prime isomorphism conjecture is accompanied by rational vanishing for compact groups, a large integral homology obstruction, solvable cases, finite-coefficient split surjectivity, integral cohomological injectivity, and low-dimensional results. The 1983 article was read and provides exact theorem-level identifications. Its proved partial statements do not settle the general Friedlander--Milnor conjecture.

speaker: André Haefliger
title: Smooth coinvariants for the modular action on the circle
summary: Haefliger asks whether every smooth function on the projective circle is a sum of the two generator coboundaries for the modular group. Exact smooth solvability is called unknown; smooth density is asserted separately. The source links the question to foliations with minimal leaves but gives no theorem making the connection precise. The companion proves exact continuous solvability, independently checked, while leaving smooth regularity unresolved. Kirillov's next heading is on P001014, outside this record.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Orbit geometry, multiplicities, and student research topics
summary: The actual heading and mathematical discussion occupy P001014--P001016; the wider catalogue range also includes Haefliger and Givental. Kirillov proposes topics on multiplicities, illustrates the geometry of an \(SU(3)\) orbit and its diagonal projection, and relates a recent Guillemin--Sternberg preprint to an index on a reduced space. Gelfand adds questions about duality, difference calculus and hypergeometric functions. The final remarks connect torus convexity with Newton polyhedra. The missing quotient in the multiplicity formula is mathematically consequential.

speaker: A. B. Givental
title: Relative symplectic normal forms and Lagrangian planes
summary: The manuscript heading is on P001017 and the talk ends on P001018. A relative Darboux theorem leads to local symplectic extension, the symplectic geometry of rays and obstacle problems, and the invariant alternating form on an odd symmetric power of the standard \(SL_2\)-module. An intervention attributed to Goldsheid asks for uniform approximation of a Lagrangian plane by a product of lines in fixed coordinate symplectic planes. That last question has much stronger quantifiers than the coordinatewise observation following it.

speaker: Mariusz Wodzicki
title: Local index densities and spectral boundary conditions
summary: The actual notes run from the heading on P001019 through P001021. Wodzicki reviews spectral zeta functions, local heat coefficients and the signature theorem, then explains the nonlocal boundary correction and spectral boundary conditions. Gelfand asks about additive invariants. The notebook mixes a closed-manifold formula with a boundary hypothesis and sketches a normal, rather than necessarily self-adjoint, tangential operator; these scopes are kept separate.

speaker: Mariusz Wodzicki
title: Eta regularity, spectral cuts, and local zeta invariants
summary: The actual heading is on P001022. The first part repeats the spectral boundary problem and discusses global versus local residues. Gelfand asks why self-adjointness and a filling should be needed. Wodzicki then compares zeta functions defined by two spectral cuts, relates their integer values to local residues, and writes a shifted-zeta formula with a missing power of the shift. The final p-adic analogy is not sufficiently specified to identify an automorphic theorem.
